title: Biography
text: Biography From aviation to signal processing My path began in Tehran with electrical engineering and aviation telecommunications. At Beihang I turned to spacecraft navigation, studying how a single image of star trails can reveal a spacecraft’s angular velocity. Today my doctoral research brings me back to signals, and to the decisions we make from them. Education 2026 – present Information & Communication Engineering School of Electronics and Information Engineering, Beihang University · Communication systems · Signal processing Supervisor · Prof. Yanhong Kou 2024 – 2026 M.Eng. in Aerospace Engineering Beihang University, Hangzhou · Space Technology Applications. Thesis on single-frame optical trail imagery for spacecraft angular velocity estimation. GPA 3.14/4.0. 2020 – 2024 B.Eng. in Electrical Engineering Civil Aviation Technology College, Tehran · Aviation telecommunications. Thesis on satellite internet in aviation. NASA Impact Visual Analysis System (NIVAS) An interactive asteroid-impact simulator using NASA and USGS data, recognized at the NASA Space Apps Challenge in Tokyo. title: Research notes
text: Research notes Signal processing Why alert timing matters Imagine a vehicle that needs two seconds to brake. If it will reach an obstacle in ten seconds, its last opportunity to start braking is at eight seconds. Raising a detector’s threshold can delay its first alert beyond that deadline. Estimating reliability would require many trajectories and a model of how they arise. Current research →
